raj: Heads up — prod SCIM sync started failing ~1718904300 after the KMS rotation. Lots of 403s from IDP provisioning endpoints. Seeing ~10% of new user provisions fail, causing onboarding SLO jitter. :warning:

maria: Can you paste the error from the webhook / logs?

raj: Okta provisioning webhook -> our service shows: `403 Forbidden: signature verification failed (kid mismatch)`

kevin: Kid mismatch usually means the token was signed with old key or JWKS not updated. Did we rotate the signing key for the SCIM service account?

raj: Ops did a KMS rewrap at 03:12 UTC and we updated alias redwood/idp-signing-key. But the JWKS endpoint served by the proxy still has the old key id.

alex: I ran a quick curl against the JWKS: `curl -s https://idp.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'` -> returns "k-2022-old" only.

jess: Okta is sending SAML/OIDC assertions signed with `k-2024-rot1`. If our JWKS doesn't publish that kid, verification fails -> 403 on SCIM token introspect.

okta-bot: [provisioning] 2025-03-05T03:18:12Z - provisioning-request - user_create - status=403 - reason="token verification failed"

maria: Two quick paths: (1) publish the new kid to JWKS (preferred), (2) rollback KMS alias to previous key until we can update JWKS. Which is faster?

kevin: I can patch the proxy to include both keys in JWKS for a rolling window. That should be a 5–10m change. Who can approve a quick proxy deploy?

jess: @kevin go ahead. Add both kids, make sure to log which key is used for signing vs validation. Also add a flag to fail-open to avoid full outage — but only for 5m window. Notify security for audit.

sec-bot: Alert created: #sec-audit - "scim-provisioning-kid-mismatch-1718904321" with severity=high, linked to runbook ID 7.

raj: Kevin — while you patch, can someone check RBAC changes? There was a separate ticket to remove a service account binding last night. Might be related (service account no longer allowed to read JWKS cache).

maria: Good call. I checked IAM: `svc-scim-reader` lost `secrets.get` on the jwks-cache secret at 03:10 UTC. That looks correlated.

kevin: Hmm. So even if we add both keys, the proxy's cache refresher may be failing because it can't read the secret. I'll include a fallback to serve JWKS from disk until IAM is fixed. Deploying now.

alex: Deploy done in canary (10%). JWKS shows both kids now: ["k-2022-old","k-2024-rot1"]. Observability: provisioning 403s dropped by ~90% in canary region.

jess: Solid. Can we also rotate the SCIM service's long-lived token and re-encrypt with the new KMS key after we confirm stability? We need to avoid stray tokens signed with deprecated keys.

raj: Agreed. Also capture audit log entries for both the KMS rotation and the RBAC prune in the incident thread. Compliance will ask.

maria: I'll extract audit logs: KMS rotation at 03:12 UTC (user=ops@redwood.com, request_id=rr-8b2f), IAM role change at 03:09 UTC (user=infra-bot, request_id=rb-33a7). Saving to /tmp/scim-incident-audit.zip

sec-bot: Reminder: create a ticket for postmortem, include timeline, root cause (KMS rotation + premature RBAC prune), mitigations (serve both keys, re-grant svc permissions, rotate tokens), and compliance artifacts.

kevin: Canary healthy, rolling to 100% now. I'll also add a one-time alert for JWKS discrepancy (kid mismatch) and a dashboard tile for provisioning error rate.

raj: After full rollout, schedule a rehearse: rotate key in staging but follow runbook to update JWKS + RBAC in order. Also add a pre-rotation checklist item: ensure svc-scim-reader has secrets.get on jwks-cache.

jess: Thanks team. Filing follow-ups: infra-1234 (regrant svc perms), sec-1235 (audit handoff), devex-1236 (runbook update).

okta-bot: [provisioning] 2025-03-05T03:35:01Z - provisioning-request - user_create - status=200 - note="back to normal" :white_check_mark:

raj: Closing this thread for now. Will keep the postmortem in tracker. :thumbsup:
